title: Rivers keep flowing into the sea, so why is the sea still salty? | So That's Why
description:
Little Q gets hit by a wave at the beach and swallows a gulp of very salty seawater. On the way home, though, she sees a fresh-water river flowing into the sea, on and on. The world's rivers pour fresh water into the sea every day, so why doesn't the sea get watered down?

In this episode, the Chief and Little Q picture the whole sea as a pot of soup that keeps simmering: first how river water carries a tiny bit of salt away from rocks in the mountains, then why the sun can carry off only the water and not the salt, and finally a dive to the seafloor to see how shells, mud and sand, hot vents and ancient salt layers take things out of seawater, and why the Red Sea is extra salty while the Baltic Sea is barely salty.

The illustrations in this episode were made with AI; they are diagrams, not measurements. The salinities, years and amounts of salt in the video are approximate figures from ocean agencies and teaching materials, and they differ from sea to sea and season to season. Seawater is very salty; please don't drink it. The source of every claim is listed in the references below.
